title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6757 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: Gold finds some relief as forced liquidations ease after Nvidia news boosts stock markets
body: Gold spiked to the upside yesterday after the news of Jensen Huang being reinstated as Nvidia CEO triggered a strong rally in equity markets. The reaction kind of confirmed the view that gold has been under pressure due to liquidations caused by stock market losses. To understand the mechanics, imagine that an investment fund holds stocks, gold and government bonds. Some stocks suddenly crash, and the fund suffers losses on leveraged positions. The fund may need to raise cash to meet margin calls, reduce leverage or satisfy investor redemptions. Rather than selling only the assets that caused the losses, it may sell whatever it can liquidate quickly. Gold is particularly useful in this situation because it is highly liquid and can be sold quickly. The Nvidia news helped reset the sentiment, which got very bearish in the final part of last week. But it doesn't really change the bigger picture. The Fed is still going to raise rates and how much will depend on the economic data and the stock market conditions. The US-Iran stalemate is still ongoing, and the situation doesn't look like it's going to improve anytime soon, with Trump continuing to signal renewed military campaign in case negotiations fail. title: CFTC staff let exchanges count bitcoin and ether toward reserves, after a 20% haircut
body: The direct price signal for BTC and ETH is small. The advisory frees up some capital on the balance sheets of crypto-native venues but doesn't create new demand for either coin. Spot ETF flows shouldn't feel it. The listed company with the most obvious stake is COIN, since Coinbase runs a CFTC-registered derivatives exchange, though the benefit is about capital efficiency rather than earnings. More broadly, it's another sign that US regulators are steadily folding crypto into existing market structure, which supports institutional sentiment more than it moves prices. --- US derivatives venues can now count some of their crypto toward operating reserves, but the haircuts, the cash-only liquidity floor and the wrong-way risk test keep that allowance modest. Summary: CFTC Staff Letter 26-31, published on 23 November, lets DCMs, SEFs and DCOs count bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins toward their 12-month operating-cost reserves. Staff won't object to minimum haircuts of 20% for bitcoin and ether and 2% for payment stablecoins. Other crypto that isn't readily marketable generally takes a 100% haircut. Crypto can't count toward the unencumbered liquid portion: at least three months of costs for SEFs and six months for DCMs and DCOs. Entities must weigh wrong-way risk, where falling crypto prices coincide with business losses. DCOs must also build liquidity risk into their haircuts and review them monthly.

title: PIMCO: AI debt and refinancing stress are splitting the corporate bond market in two
body: The split points to rising default and restructuring risk among CCC-rated borrowers, particularly in technology, media, telecoms and consumer sectors, even without a recession. That's a warning for holders of lower-quality junk debt and for leveraged loan markets. In investment grade, heavy AI issuance from hyperscalers is likely to keep pressure on top-rated tech bonds, while scarce non-AI credit stays in demand. The trend also ties AI's financing needs more closely to bond-market conditions: if issuance slows after the midterms, AA spreads could recover. A sharper economic slowdown is the main risk, since investment grade spreads can widen quickly once growth fears take hold. --- In corporate bonds, the AI boom is crowding the top of the ratings ladder while high interest rates squeeze the bottom, and PIMCO says those are two separate problems.

title: The U.S. housing market is in a 'deep freeze' — and the AI boom isn't helping
body: Strip away the AI spending boom and high interest rates are leaving a serious mark on the real economy. That is the core takeaway from a new Hot Charts note from National Bank of Canada Senior Economist Jocelyn Paquet, who describes the U.S. real estate market as being stuck in a "deep freeze". It's not hard to see why. Higher borrowing costs since the pandemic have crushed affordability and pushed would-be buyers to the sidelines. The average U.S. 30-year fixed mortgage rate is sitting in the 7.15% to 7.41% range, about 100 bps above a year ago. Rather than thawing out, the data shows things are actually getting worse: The pending home sales index dropped to the lowest level of transactions in its history in October. Conditions are marginally better, but soft demand has pushed new-home inventory near its highest level since the Great Recession. Permits fell in October to their lowest level since the pandemic. The NAHB Housing Market Index tumbled in November to its lowest reading since 2012. For homebuilders, the problem isn't just that buyers are sitting on their hands or that financing is expensive. They are also getting squeezed hard on the cost side. National Bank's chart on Producer Price Index categories shows that inputs to residential construction have surged nearly 60% since the pandemic began—vastly outpacing headline PPI.

title: Bank of Canada may need to respond sooner or more forcefully to major supply shocks
body: Comments from Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem and highlights from the Bank's summary of its renewed monetary policy framework crossed the wires. Bank of Canada may need to respond sooner or more forcefully when supply shocks are large, persistent or broad-based. BoC may also need forceful response if demand is strong, or when businesses and households begin to expect higher inflation will persist. Monetary policy decisions should rely on richer evidence, scenario analysis and judgment, rather than on any single model or measure of inflation. Participants in BoC survey indicated they would be willing to tolerate inflation slightly above 2% if it meant people kept jobs and businesses kept running. Deciding in real time whether to look through a shock or respond to it requires a risk management mindset. BoC is therefore investing in models that can better assess supply shocks and capture dynamics of pricing decisions. Monetary policy can temporarily influence housing demand but cannot address supply constraints. Renewed framework drops all mentions of Bank using the 1%–3% target range to seek maximum sustainable employment when conditions warrant. End-year inflation may not be quite as high as the roughly 3.5% the Bank of Canada predicted in October. Businesses are set to pass through more costs to consumers and this second-round effect of the oil shock will add to inflation persistence. Economy has shown more resilience than we expected.

title: What is a short squeeze and why can it trigger violent rallies?
body: A short squeeze occurs when investors who have bet against an asset are forced to buy it back as prices move higher, accelerating the rally. It is essentially a feedback loop in which rising prices trigger additional buying, pushing prices even higher. To understand how it works, imagine an investor who borrows shares of a company and sells them at $100, expecting the price to fall. The investor plans to buy them back later at a lower price, return the borrowed shares and pocket the difference. However, if the stock moves higher instead, the short position starts generating losses. Unlike a traditional long position, where the maximum loss is limited to the initial investment, short positions have theoretically unlimited downside because there is no ceiling on how high a stock can rise. As losses accumulate, short sellers may face margin calls or decide to close their positions to prevent further losses. To do so, they must buy back the shares they previously sold. This creates additional demand, pushing prices up further and forcing even more short sellers to cover. This is what makes short squeezes so violent. The buying is driven not only by investors who want to own the asset, but also by traders who are forced to exit losing positions quickly. The resulting demand can become self-reinforcing, producing sharp rallies that are disproportionate to any improvement in fundamentals.

title: Australia CPI preview: 4.8% looks like the peak, but the core print will move the RBA
body: The headline rise is largely priced in, so the Australian dollar and short-dated Australian government bond yields are more exposed to the core reading. The Aussie is trading around 66.4 US cents. A trimmed mean of 0.4% or firmer would likely lift front-end yields and support the currency by pushing back expectations for the first rate cut. A 0.3% print would leave in place the banks' expected easing timeline for mid-to-late 2027. US markets are heading into a Thanksgiving-shortened week, so any AUD move may meet thinner liquidity than usual. For energy watchers, the fuel-led headline is another sign of crude prices feeding into inflation and central bank decisions well beyond the US. Summary: October CPI is due at 00:30 GMT Wednesday (7:30pm US Eastern Tuesday) Headline is expected up 0.4% m/m, taking the annual rate to 4.8% from 4.3% Trimmed mean forecasts split between 0.3% m/m (3.6% y/y) and 0.4% m/m (3.7% y/y) Higher fuel prices and the unwinding of electricity subsidies are the main headline drivers The 1 October ban on card surcharges is an uncertain upside risk to core prices The RBA cash rate is 4.85% after a 6-3 vote to hike in November, and markets see a December hold as near certain Australia's October consumer price index, due at 00:30 GMT on Wednesday (7:30pm US Eastern on Tuesday), is expected to show headline inflation at what forecasters see as the top of the current cycle.

title: Euro futures rebound as German business confidence hits 90.6.
body: Euro futures posted an inside range day, advancing for the third time in nine sessions. The contract traded between a low of 1.0905 and a high of 1.09895, gaining 0.57% late in the trading session. Fundamental support arrived from Germany, where business confidence improved for a seventh consecutive month. The Ifo Business Climate Index climbed to 90.6 in November, signaling to market participants that the eurozone's largest economy and the broader region are holding up better than previously anticipated. Hawkish commentary from European Central Bank officials also drew trader attention. ECB Governing Council member Gediminas Simkus stated that policymakers should act sooner rather than later, noting that a weaker euro adds to inflation pressure and that the risk of overtightening remains limited. ECB President Christine Lagarde also noted that the eurozone economy is performing better than expected, keeping market focus on the rate differential with the U.S.

title: 10-Year T-Note futures climbed in 6 of the last 7 sessions.
body: 10-Year T-Note futures extended their upward momentum, recording gains in six of the last seven trading sessions. Prices traded near 106'27 after challenging the 107'00 handle intraday. Recent volatility in equity markets and softer economic data points have influenced Treasury market sentiment, as participants evaluate whether the Federal Reserve will reconsider its recent hawkish tone. Market focus now turns to the upcoming Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, due later this week. In the cash market, the 10-Year Treasury Note yield declined 1 bps to hover near 4.90%. The broader yield curve flattened slightly on the back end, with yields moving lower from the 3-Year to the 30-Year maturities while the 2-Year yield remained largely unchanged.
